key_headlines.title: South Korea Raises 2026 Growth Forecast to 3% on Semiconductor Boom
key_headlines.summary: The government upgraded its economic growth outlook from 2.0% to 3.0%, reflecting strong semiconductor exports and investment. However, employment gains are expected to slow to 150,000 people, highlighting concerns about jobless growth and widening income inequality.

key_headlines.title: Bank of Korea Likely to Raise Base Rate to 2.75% Amid Inflation Concerns
key_headlines.summary: The central bank is expected to raise interest rates on July 16th with market focus shifting to timing of additional increases. Year-end rate expectations have risen to 3% amid strong inflation and export data.

key_headlines.title: South Korea to Invest 1,350 Trillion Won in Semiconductors and AI Data Centers
key_headlines.summary: The government plans to invest 800 trillion won in fourth semiconductor fab in southwestern region and 550 trillion won in AI data centers as part of efforts to secure technological supremacy. The Korea Investment Corporation will establish a strategic investment division.

key_headlines.title: U.S. Federal Reserve Chair Powell Commits to Controlling Inflation Despite Rate Pressure
key_headlines.summary: Fed Chair Kevin Powell testified that the central bank will not tolerate high inflation and remains committed to price stability. Powell avoided committing to specific rate path decisions while maintaining the Fed's independence from political pressure.

key_headlines.title: Crude Oil Surges 10% as Trump Announces Iran Maritime Blockade
key_headlines.summary: International oil prices jumped nearly 10% following U.S. President Trump's announcement of renewed blockade of Iranian maritime routes. Brent crude exceeded $83 per barrel, raising inflation concerns and potentially forcing the Fed to maintain higher rates.

sections.Hot Economy News: South Korea's economy is gaining momentum on the back of a semiconductor supercycle, with the government raising its 2026 growth forecast to 3.0% from 2.0%, reflecting unprecedented semiconductor export prosperity. However, structural challenges persist including jobless growth with employment gains downwardly revised to 150,000 people and widening inequality between semiconductors and non-semiconductor sectors. The government is implementing expansionary fiscal policy worth 800 trillion won alongside major infrastructure projects to spread semiconductor benefits across the broader economy. Key concerns include the three-high problem (high interest rates, high exchange rates, high prices) and risks that the semiconductor tailwind may not transmit to domestic demand if not properly managed.
sections.Macro & Fiscal Policy: The Bank of Korea is expected to raise the base rate to 2.75% on July 16th amid strengthening inflation data and export performance, with market consensus expecting year-end rates around 3%. The government is pursuing an 800 trillion won expansionary fiscal policy to support growth and address employment challenges, though coordination concerns exist with the monetary tightening cycle. The U.S. Federal Reserve signaled inflation remains a priority despite recent cooling CPI data, with Chair Powell emphasizing the Fed will not tolerate persistently high inflation. Geopolitical tensions, including potential oil supply disruptions from Iran, pose additional upside risks to inflation globally and domestically.
sections.Financial Markets: The Korean stock market showed volatility with KOSPI closing up 0.73% at 6,856.83 points, while the won-dollar exchange rate stood at 1,493 won per dollar amid mixed signals. U.S. Treasury yields surged above 4.6% on oil price spikes related to Iran tensions, though earlier CPI disappointment temporarily reduced Fed rate increase expectations from 42% to 17%. Corporate cost pressures are mounting from converging headwinds of tariffs, high exchange rates, elevated interest rates, rising labor costs, and input price inflation. Semiconductor stocks rebounded on reduced near-term Fed rate increase expectations, though long-term uncertainty remains around geopolitical risk.
sections.Industry & Technology: South Korea's SK On began mass production of electric vehicle batteries at its U.S. joint venture facility with Hyundai Motor in Georgia, with capacity for 35 gigawatt-hours annually supporting approximately 300,000 EVs. The automotive industry is intensifying competition to secure semiconductor supplies as electric vehicles now require around 1,000 semiconductors per vehicle, driving strategic alliances between car and chip makers. Specialty electronic materials companies are gaining strategic importance as the semiconductor and electric vehicle industries become increasingly dependent on high-purity, high-functionality materials for next-generation products. The petrochemical industry is gaining recognition for its essential role in producing medical supplies, packaging, battery materials, and semiconductor components vital to modern manufacturing and healthcare.
sections.Real Estate: The government is expanding the jeonse deposit trust system to prevent deposit fraud, though mandatory implementation risks accelerating the shift from jeonse to monthly rentals. Real estate sector discussions continue on tax policy reforms including capital gains tax bases and taxation standards for ultra-high-value properties, with disagreements over threshold definitions ranging from 3 billion to 10 billion won. Housing supply expansion forums are addressing competing interests between construction industry calls for regulatory relief and civil society concerns about tenant protections and public rental housing expansion. Real estate policy tensions persist between ensuring affordability and stability while encouraging adequate housing supply through market mechanisms.
sections.International Economy: U.S. President Trump announced renewed maritime blockade of Iranian oil exports and conducted additional airstrikes, sending crude oil prices surging 10% and raising global inflation concerns. Fed Chair Powell's congressional testimony emphasized the central bank's independence and commitment to controlling inflation despite political pressure for rate cuts, though the specific policy path remains data-dependent. Market expectations shifted dramatically from 42% probability of July Fed rate increase to just 17% following softer U.S. CPI data, though geopolitical oil supply risks complicate the inflation outlook. The Fed faces conflicting signals between moderating price pressures and external supply shocks that could reignite inflation, delaying expected rate cuts.
sections.AI & Economy: Leading global economists and AI researchers, including 16 Nobel Prize winners, released a joint statement emphasizing urgent action is needed to establish safeguards and institutional frameworks to ensure AI benefits society while managing risks. The statement warns that AI transformation could be even more dramatic than the Industrial Revolution but compressed into a much shorter timeframe, potentially enabling massive productivity gains but also requiring proactive policy responses. South Korea is incorporating AI considerations into employment policy reforms to address labor market disruption from automation and platform-based work arrangements. The government is prioritizing AI data center investment as part of its semiconductor-led growth strategy to maintain technological competitiveness in the emerging AI infrastructure economy.
sections.Others: The Korean securities industry is implementing measures to reduce concentration risk in single-stock leverage ETFs by raising minimum deposit requirements and promoting portfolio diversification, responding to recent investor losses and market volatility. U.S. military operations against Iran include deployment of over 20 naval vessels and hundreds of military aircraft to enforce maritime blockade and economic pressure through crude oil export restrictions. Concerns are rising among retail investors about leverage ETF risks, with financial experts proposing warning system frameworks similar to traffic signals to communicate investment danger levels. The Korea Chamber of Commerce and Industry celebrated its 80th anniversary, pledging to support member companies' international expansion and adaptation to AI-driven economic transformation.
